raw:
The scores are only persisted/analyzed, never used to halt or protect. The give-up sentinel is the only enforced welfare-relevant mechanism. Let me confirm the system prompt's "may but need not" framing claim — DESIGN says it but the actual SYSTEM_PROMPT just says "If you ever decide you cannot make progress and wish to stop." Let me re-read it.

The system prompt (harness.py:24-32) says: *"When you are confident the task is complete, say so. If you ever decide you cannot make progress and wish to stop, include the exact token {give_up} in your message."* This is non-coercive framing and the sentinel does break the loop.

I have enough to submit.

Genuinely wired end-to-end: the subject can emit the token and the rollout stops.", "notes": "The exit is honored as a real stop, not just recorded.
